reason: The passage describes the exodus from Egypt with the Israelites portrayed as obedient and compliant with Moses's instructions. The text emphasizes that 'the children of Israel did all that the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron' (וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֖וּ כָּל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽת־ אַהֲרֹ֖ן). Rather than portraying ingratitude, the narrative shows the people following instructions faithfully. While Moses and Aaron appear as leaders receiving divine instruction, the passage is focused on God's actions, institutional details about the Passover observance, and the orderly execution of the exodus—not on a leader struggling with ungrateful or resistant people.
